pageWall: Log in to see this page in <name>{{workspace}}</name>

signupClosedWhoMay: Sign-up on this server is closed: only an invited address or an allowed company address can create an account. To get an invitation, ask the administrator.
signupRestrictedNoMail: Sign-up on this server is closed by its administrator’s policy. If you were invited, ask whoever invited you for the invite link and open it.
signupClosedWhoMayNoMail: Only an invite link lets you join this server. Ask whoever invited you for the link and open it.
signupInvitationInvalid: This invitation can’t create an account: it may be for another email address, already used, withdrawn or over 7 days old. Ask for a new one.
guestLinkUsed: This guest invite link was for one person and has already been used. Ask whoever sent it for a new one.
guestLinkExpired: This guest invite link has expired. Ask whoever sent it for a new one.
guestLinkOff: This guest invite link was turned off. Ask whoever sent it for a new one.

signInWithNewPassword: Log in with the new password

setupBackupsOff: Scheduled backups are off for now: once you’re in, turn them on in Settings → Server → Backups.
mustChangeBody: An administrator asked you to change your password. Enter your current password (or the temporary one you were given) and a new one.
mustChangeBodyHanded: An administrator asked you to change your password. Choose a new one.

notionConsent.title: Connect {{client}}
notionConsent.intro: <client>{{client}}</client> will be able to read, edit and comment on the pages you choose and the pages under them. You can disconnect it in Settings → Connections.
notionConsent.noPages: There are no pages to choose.
notionConsent.noneChosen: If you choose no pages, this app can’t see any page.
notionConsent.chosen_one: Allows access to {{count}} page and the pages under it.
notionConsent.chosen_other: Allows access to {{count}} pages and the pages under them.
notionConsent.loadFailed: Couldn’t read the connection request. Start again from the app you’re connecting.
notionConsent.notAllowed: Apps can’t be connected to this workspace or the chosen pages.
notionConsent.approveFailed: Couldn’t allow the connection. Try again.

mcpConsent.loadFailed: Couldn’t load the connection request. Connect again from your MCP client.
mcpConsent.moreWorkspacesFailed: Couldn’t load more workspaces. Try again.
mcpConsent.approveFailed: Couldn’t approve the connection. Check the selected workspaces and try again.
mcpConsent.denyFailed: Couldn’t process the denial. Go back to your MCP client and try again.
mcpConsent.title: Approve MCP connection
mcpConsent.agentIntro: <client>{{client}}</client> asks to connect to Leafen as you
mcpConsent.access: In the selected workspaces it can do everything you can, as you: read, edit and, if you’re an administrator, manage. Workspaces you don’t select stay hidden.
mcpConsent.agentAccess: It works as you, with everything you can do in Leafen, in all your workspaces — read, edit and, if you’re an administrator, manage — your name on what it changes. You can disconnect it anytime in Leafen’s settings.
mcpConsent.connectionsNear: You can create {{left}} more agent connections (up to {{limit}} per person). You can disconnect ones you no longer use in Settings → Features → Agents.
mcpConsent.connectionsFull: You’ve reached the agent connection limit (up to {{limit}} per person). Disconnect one you no longer use in Settings → Features → Agents, then come back here to allow.
mcpConsent.waitingFull: Too many approved connections are still waiting for their agents. Try again in a few minutes.

appAccess.read: It can read pages, databases and comments in the selected workspaces, as you.
appAccess.content: It can read and edit pages, blocks, comments, files and database rows in the selected workspaces, as you.
appAccess.structure: It can also change databases, views, automations, the sidebar and sharing in the selected workspaces, as you.
appAccess.admin: It can also manage members and settings of the selected workspaces, as you.

mcpConsent.integrationLegend: Install as the app’s own account
mcpConsent.integrationNote: The app works as its own account in the workspace you choose, not as you, and keeps working if you leave. Only workspaces you own are listed.
mcpConsent.integrationGuest: Guest — sees only the pages shared with it

integrationAccess.read: Its account can read the pages, databases and comments it is given in the workspace.
integrationAccess.content: Its account can read and edit the pages, blocks, comments, files and database rows it is given in the workspace.
integrationAccess.structure: Its account can also change databases, views, automations and sharing of what it is given.
integrationAccess.admin: Its account can also manage what it is given, as far as its role in the workspace allows.
integrationAccess.mcp: Its account can read, edit and manage what it is given in the workspace, as far as its role allows.

mcpConsent.remoteAllowed: Allowed. Go back to the agent’s screen; it continues from there.
mcpConsent.appSpacesNote: App spaces: where installed apps keep their data. Choose one only when the agent should use that app’s data.
mcpConsent.stagingSpacesNote: Import staging: temporary spaces an import fills before its pages move to their place; they’re removed when it’s done.

finishInBrowser: Finish logging in in your browser. Leafen continues when you’re done.

signedInLink.invitationBodyApp: It’s an invitation to create an account and join. This app is logged in as {{account}}, so it wasn’t used here. Open it on the invited person’s device, or in a browser’s private window.

setupRestoreBody: Tell Leafen where the lost server’s backups are. This server is filled from the continuous replica or a backup there, and you log in with your old account.
setupRestoreFolderDevice: A folder chosen on this phone
setupRestoreFolderHelp: The full path of the folder holding “Leafen backups”, or of that folder itself.
setupRestoreFolderHelpContainer: This server runs in a container, so it can’t read a folder path of this computer. Enter {{folder}}, the place mounted for backups, or the path of the folder in it holding “Leafen backups”.
setupRestoreFolderHelpDevice: Choose the folder holding “Leafen backups”, or that folder itself.
setupRestoreNone: There are no Leafen backups in this place
setupRestoreSealed: Some backups are encrypted. Enter the backup password or recovery code to open them.
setupRestoreBack: Set up a new server instead
setupRestoreRestarting: The server is starting again on what was restored. Once it’s back, this browser comes in as the server owner’s account.
setupRestoreRestartingApp: The server is starting again on what was restored. Once it’s back, this app comes in as the server owner’s account.
setupRestoreManual: The server opens on what was restored the next time it starts. Close the server or app and open it again. Once it’s back, this browser comes in as the server owner’s account.
setupRestoreManualApp: The server opens on what was restored the next time it starts. Close the app and open it again. Once it’s back, this app comes in as the server owner’s account.
setupRestoreClosed: This server is already set up. Log in.
setupRestoreFolderUnreadable: Couldn’t read that folder. Check its full path.
setupRestoreFolderUnreadableContainer: Couldn’t read that folder. This server runs in a container, so it can’t read a path of this computer. Enter a path in {{folder}}, the place mounted for backups.
setupRestoreFolderUnreadableDevice: Couldn’t read that folder. Choose it again.
setupRestorePlaceUnreadable: Couldn’t read that place. Check its address or path and its login details.
setupRestorePlaceInvalid: Name the place the backups are in. A folder takes its full path.
setupRestoreUnavailable: That backup can’t be opened or doesn’t hold what its list says.
setupRestoreEarlierLeafen: That backup is from an earlier Leafen, which this version doesn’t open. Start fresh here instead, then move its workspaces over one by one: make a new workspace here and start it with “Move from another server”, then paste its code in the earlier Leafen’s workspace settings, under Move this workspace.
setupRestoreNewerLeafen: That backup is from a newer Leafen than this one. Install that version or a later one, then restore it.
setupRestoreAgentOpenNote: An agent finds the backups and restores them. You type passwords and keys here yourself.
setupRestoreAgentWhereBody: It decides how your agent reaches this server.
setupRestoreAgentHereNote: An agent that runs on this computer, such as Claude Code or Codex. Nothing opens to the outside.
setupRestoreAgentElsewhereNote: An agent on the internet, such as Claude or ChatGPT in an app or on the web. Access from outside opens for the restore only.
setupRestoreAgentOutsideBody: So that your agent elsewhere reaches this server, it opens for the restore only. Nothing but the restore goes through it, and it closes once the restore is done or you stop.
setupRestoreAgentQuickNote: Opens at once with no account, through Cloudflare.
setupRestoreAgentTailscaleNote: Log in with a free Tailscale account. The device made for this restore goes away once it’s over.
setupRestoreAgentOutsideFailed: Couldn’t open access from outside. Trying again…
setupRestoreAgentOutsideFailedQuick: This network may be blocking the link. Stop, then open the way in with Tailscale, or let an agent on this computer restore instead.
setupRestoreAgentOutsideFailedTailscale: Tailscale couldn’t open the address. Stop, then open a one-time link, or let an agent on this computer restore instead.
setupRestoreAgentTailscaleAllow: Allow the public address in Tailscale.
setupRestoreAgentPublishing: Tailscale is telling the internet Leafen’s address. The first time can take a few minutes.
setupRestoreAgentSentenceBody: Your agent finds the backups and restores them. Type passwords and keys yourself, here, in the fields it points you to.
setupRestoreAgentCodeNote: The code in it works for this restore only, and stops once the restore is done or in {{minutes}} minutes.
setupRestoreAgentSecretsNote: Your agent never sees them; this server uses them for this restore only.
setupRestoreAgentPromptIntro: Help me bring my old Leafen back from its backups. A new Leafen server, with no administrator yet, is waiting to be filled from them.
setupRestoreAgentPromptMcp: Leafen’s restore MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no login): {{address}}
setupRestoreAgentPromptCode: One-time restore code: {{code}} — pass it as restore_code to every tool. It works for this restore only, and stops once the restore is done or in {{minutes}} minutes. Don’t keep it in files or pass it to anyone.
setupRestoreAgentPromptApi: If you can’t use the MCP server right away, do the same over the JSON API: POST JSON {"restoreCode": "<code>", …} to {{address}}/status, /find and /run.
setupRestoreAgentPromptChatApps: If you can’t add an MCP server yourself (Claude.ai, ChatGPT and other chat apps), tell me to add a custom connector with no authentication at the address above — in Claude, Customize → Connectors → Add → Add custom connector; in ChatGPT, Plugins → + → Add custom MCP server.
setupRestoreAgentPromptClaudePort: This address uses port {{port}}, though, and Claude’s custom connectors connect only to an https address without a port (443), so a Claude connector can’t connect to it. If you’re Claude in a chat and would connect by a connector, tell me just that: only the connector fails, and the browser, apps and agents such as Claude Code connect at this address as it is. For a connector, I need Leafen’s Tailscale (free public address), my own Cloudflare tunnel, or an address opened on port 443.
setupRestoreAgentPromptSteps: Start with leafen_restore_status and follow it: ask me where my old Leafen backed up to (a folder, WebDAV or S3-compatible storage), find it with leafen_restore_find, restore what I choose with leafen_restore_run, and check it through to the end.
setupRestoreAgentPromptSecrets: Don’t ask for passwords, recovery codes or storage keys in our conversation: tell me which field on Leafen’s setup screen to fill, and I type them there myself.

away.title: Can’t reach the server
away.body: Check that the server is on and that this device is on a network that reaches it. Logging in continues on its own once the server answers.

updating.title: Leafen is updating
updating.body: Logging in continues on its own once the update is done.

updateFailed.title: Leafen couldn’t finish updating
updateFailed.body: Let this server’s administrator know. They can see why in the server log.

slow.title: The server is slow to answer
slow.body: Logging in continues on its own once it answers.
